newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Paranagua workers yet to decide on strike.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Paranagua workers yet to decide on strike.

text.p: Stevedores at the key Brazilian grain loading port of Paranagua have yet to decide whether to join in a possible national port strike this week, an official said.
"Our president has gone to Santos and from that meeting he will draw his conclusions and bring them to us tomorrow," said an official at the Paranagua Stevedores' Union.
Delegates of the National Stevedores' Union are scheduled to meet at Santos port at 1400 local/1700 GMT to decide whether a current strike at the port should spread nationally.
Stevedores at Santos are protesting steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) using its own workers to load and unload vessels at its private terminal at the port.

During a similar strike last week, stevedores at Paranagua stopped work for an hour in solidarity with their colleagues at Santos, but the protest had no effect on the loading of grains, which consists mostly of soybeans and soy products.

A spokeswoman for the port said it was likely any renewed protest would take a similar form, pointing out that the Paranagua stevedores had resolved a local labor dispute which triggered a strike there in March.
But she said moves were afoot for companies with private terminals at Paranagua to also start using their own workers.
"So far we have nothing official, but the intention is there," she said. "There are comments, there is no formal declaration."

Although neither unions nor the port authority have made any comments to the effect, the precedent set by Santos indicates any attempt by private terminals at Paranagua to stop using unionized labor could lead to fresh strikes.
